subject: MAP: Acceptance protocol, exit gates & evaluation scenarios — Redwood <> HealthPort
messages:
From: Hannah Schmitt <hannah.schmitt@redwood.com>
To: Elena Morales <elena@healthport.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-11-30T09:12:00-08:00
Subject: MAP kickoff — acceptance protocol, exit gates & evaluation scenarios

Hi Elena — great to meet last week. Per our call, I put together a lean MAP focused on what HealthPort needs to validate in the pilot so we can move to a production contract. Attached: HP_MAP_v1.xlsx (mutual action plan) and a short acceptance-tests doc. Key asks up front:

- Decision window: 6-week pilot starting 2026-12-06; target close week of 2027-01-17.
- Exit gates (high level):
  1) Latency SLA: 95th pctile < 350ms for common flows
  2) Accuracy concordance: > 92% for anonymized extraction tasks vs. your gold set
  3) Data handling: KV cache disabled for PHI routes; access logs available to you
  4) Ops: runbook + rollback plan tested in staging with two simulated failures

Can you confirm the timeline and whether procurement wants the MAP in a different format? I called out owners in the sheet; happy to iterate.

Next steps I propose:
- You share the security SAQ (if you have one) — we can return evidence within 72 hours
- Redwood will deliver a test harness (sample dataset + scripts) by 2026-12-03
- Weekly syncs on Tuesdays, 30 minutes (first: 2026-12-08)

Thanks,
Hannah

Hi Hannah — thanks, this looks like a strong start. A couple quick clarifications from a security/procurement perspective:

- I've attached our security SAQ (HealthPort_Security_SAQ.pdf). Please confirm who on your team will own each evidence item and expected delivery dates.
- Latency gate: we need to ensure the 95th pctl is measured from our east-coast region (I listed that in the SAQ). Will Redwood provide region-specific profiling?
- For accuracy concordance, we'll provide a goldset (anonymized) and expect a repeatable scoring script; can your test harness accept CSV + a scoring script?

Procurement (cc'd): can you confirm what contractual term length you prefer for a pilot? Historically we do 90-day pilots, but commercial would accept 6-week if there's a defined acceptance & close plan.

Subject: Re: MAP kickoff — acceptance protocol, exit gates & evaluation scenarios

Elena — thanks for the SAQ, received. Quick replies inline and delivery commitments below.

- Evidence ownership: Marissa (cc) will own the evidence pack and coordinate with your security team. We can provide evidence for the majority of typical SAQ items in 48–72 hours; for items requiring logs from Private deployments we'll mark those as "TBD" until staging is online.
- Region profiling: yes — runtime supports regional benches. We'll run the 95th-pctl test from us-east-1 and from our west coast cluster to validate variance. Delivery: profiling report by 2026-12-10.
- Test harness: we can accept CSV + your scoring script. We'll run the scoring in an isolated environment and publish the raw outputs and the concordance script.

Acceptance-tests summary (high level):
- Test A (Functional): end-to-end extraction on goldset — pass if F1 >= 0.92 across the sample
- Test B (Performance): 95th pctl latency < 350ms from us-east — pass at < 350ms
- Test C (Stability): 72-hour soak with no more than 0.5% error rate
- Test D (Security): SAQ evidence delivered + one successful audit log export

Proposed pilot timeline (updated):
- 2026-12-03: Redwood test harness delivered (csv + run script)
- 2026-12-06: Pilot start (data flows unblinded for acceptance tests)
- 2026-12-20: Acceptance test window closes (two-week run window)
- 2026-12-22 — 2027-01-05: Buffer for remediation and a second verification run if needed
- 2027-01-10: Target signoff and contract execution week (DocuSign link in MAP)

I'll attach a short acceptance-tests doc to this thread tonight. If procurement prefers a 90-day pilot, we can add an extension clause in the MAP; we'll flag what acceptance gates move into the extension vs. the initial run.

Thanks — Hannah

Attachment stubs: Redwood_Acceptance-Tests_v1.docx

From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>

Subject: Re: MAP kickoff — acceptance protocol, exit gates & evaluation scenarios

Elena / Hannah — quick operational note from my side on the acceptance-tests doc: I added concrete measurement methods so there's no ambiguity. Highlights:

- Latency: We will run a synthetic replay of N=5k requests sampling your typical distribution; measurement collected at the gateway and at the model side. The MAP includes the scripts used for sampling.
- Concordance scoring: We will store both raw predictions and scoring outputs in a shared bucket with 30-day retention for the pilot; HealthPort will have read access.
- Failure-mode test: We propose two injected faults during the staging run (one network flake, one model restart) and verify RTO < 5 minutes.

If that aligns, I'll update the MAP spreadsheet with owners/dates and export a PDF version for procurement.

— Marissa
Product Ops | Redwood Inference
marissa.cole@redwood.com

Hannah / Marissa — procurement looped me in. HealthPort is OK with the 6-week pilot but asks two contract-side clarifications:

We can sign off on the MAP once those items are noted in the mutual action plan and a DocuSign is created. Procurement, can you confirm if we need a PO for the pilot or if a signed MSA addendum will suffice?
